title: Inspect a disc brake
summary: Inspect rotor condition, caliper alignment and contamination risks without opening the hydraulic system.

tools.name: Brake-safe isopropyl alcohol
tools.note: For rotor cleaning only when appropriate.

steps.title: Inspect the rotor
steps.instruction: Rotate the wheel slowly and look for visible side-to-side rotor movement, scoring, cracks or obvious heat damage.
steps.why: Rotor defects can cause rubbing, poor braking or unsafe operation.
steps.warning: Do not touch the braking surface with oily fingers.
steps.check: No cracks or obviously unsafe rotor damage are visible.

steps.title: Check rotor-to-caliper alignment
steps.instruction: Look through the caliper and compare the rotor clearance on both sides. Rotate the wheel and note any repeated contact.
steps.why: Unequal clearance or periodic rubbing can indicate caliper misalignment or rotor runout.
steps.check: Rotor passes through the caliper without continuous rubbing.

steps.title: Check for contamination
steps.instruction: Inspect rotor and caliper area for oil, grease or other contamination. Keep lubricants away from pads and rotor.
steps.why: Disc-brake friction surfaces are highly sensitive to contamination.
steps.warning: Do not apply chain lubricant, penetrating oil or general-purpose cleaners near the braking surfaces.

steps.title: Perform a controlled functional check
steps.instruction: After visual inspection, confirm normal lever feel and braking response in a safe low-speed test before normal riding.
steps.why: A static inspection cannot prove braking performance under load.
steps.warning: If braking feels abnormal, stop using the bicycle until the cause is identified or professionally serviced.
steps.check: Brake engages predictably and releases without abnormal drag.
